svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.14.3.3 Installation
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.14 DRAINAGE
Installation

g.text: Laid on undisturbed or well-compacted soil
Red dashes: bottom of the floor slab. Top of
the tile or pipe below it
Butt joints left open 6 mm to 10 mm
Top half of each joint covered: sheathing
Top and sides: not less than 150 mm (5⅞″)
of crushed stone or coarse clean granular
material, max. 10% passing a 4 mm sieve

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Drain tile or pipe is laid on undisturbed or
well-compacted soil so that its top is below
the bottom of the floor slab or the ground
cover of the crawl space
Drain tile or pipe with butt joints is laid
with 6 mm to 10 mm (¼″ to ⅜″) open joints
The top half of those joints is covered with
sheathing paper, 0.10 mm (3.9 mil)
polyethylene or No. 15 asphalt or
tar-saturated felt
The top and sides of drain pipe or tile are
covered with not less than 150 mm (5⅞″) of
crushed stone or other coarse clean granular
material
Containing not more than 10% of material that
will pass a 4 mm sieve.
Drawn: B and C show clay tile lengths on soil. Joint gaps and cover thickness are exaggerated.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.14.3.3. (page 9-115)
Metric values quoted from the code · imperial in brackets converted · ACCESS Trades
